prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Distributed Systems Glossary (language en).
Grid: 3 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Term" · longest unbreakable word 87px · one-line width 135px
  col 2: header "Definition" · longest unbreakable word 95px · one-line width 1303px
  col 3: header "Example" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 721px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 565px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 564px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Help readers understand distributed-systems terms through definitions and examples.","reading":"Readers scan the first column for a term, then read across the row to connect its definition with an example; they may also compare definitions or examples down a column.","groups":["Definition and Example are companion prose columns: one explains the concept and the other illustrates it.","Term is the row identifier and should remain easy to scan independently."],"keep_intact":["Unbreakable technical words and identifiers","Term labels where practical"],"may_wrap":["Definitions and examples at natural word boundaries","Multiword terms when needed; their wrapping can fit within the height created by longer prose"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [116, 270, 178] · table 565×850px · row heights [33, 114, 114, 114, 114, 114, 114, 134] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [120, 280, 164] · table 565×891px · row heights [33, 114, 134, 114, 134, 114, 114, 134] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [120, 260, 184] · table 565×850px · row heights [33, 114, 114, 114, 114, 114, 114, 134] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
